propositions: Cross-subtree blocking link escalation substitutes the requested edge silently; the CLI sees the redirect record via stdout but library and MCP callers receive only 'ok' with no indication the endpoints were changed
The redirect record is composed and printed to stdout via _emit_redirect but never returned, so it is discarded by quiet=True context managers wrapping library calls and MCP tool invocations

Five layers in the propagation chain (_links.add_dependency -> composer.link_core -> _lib_writes._link -> _lib_writes._python_leaf -> _lib_writes.rebar.link) drop the return value; three of these are drop points that must be fixed for the record to reach callers

Removing quiet=True would corrupt the MCP-over-stdio protocol by injecting unsuppressed print output into the JSON-RPC stream, and would break stdout suppression needed by the reconciler, code-review finalizer, and review-bot voter
The fix must return the redirect record as a value through all five layers while preserving quiet=True and the existing stdout print for CLI contracts
Library and MCP callers must be able to detect when escalation occurred; MCP link_tickets must return a string template reporting the original and resolved endpoints when substitution happens
